newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: China escapes censure at UN human rights body.
newsitem.headline: China escapes censure at UN human rights body.

text.p: For the seventh year in a row, China on Tuesday averted censure at the United Nations Human Rights Commission by succesfully quashing a Western resolution critical of its record.
The 53-member forum approved a "no-action motion", tabled by China, by a vote of 27 countries in favour, 17 countries against with nine abstentions, according to the chairman's tally.
Delegates erupted into applause when the vote -- nearly identical to last year's result -- was announced after more than 90 minutes of sometimes acrimonious debate.

Wu Jianmen, China's ambassador to the United Nations in Geneva who heads his country's delegation, tabled the "no-action" motion and fiercely denounced the Western resolution, tabled by Denmark with backing from 14 countries including the United States.

It was, Wu declared, "a tool of power politics directed not just against China but also against all developing countries." In the later vote, Beijing won the support of the overwhelming majority of Third World states on the Commission.

Assistant U.S. Secretary of State John Shattuck and British delegate Henry Steel objected to the Chinese "no action" manoeuvre. Shattuck said the rights situation in China was "a subject of considerable concern" although Washington did not seek confrontation with Beijing.
